headline: Committees to prevent drugs and gambling formed in all educational institutions
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has decided to form committees in all educational institutions across the country to combat drug abuse and gambling. This initiative aims to ensure a safe and healthy educational environment for students.
details: The Ministry of Home Affairs has decided to form committees in all educational institutions across the country to prevent drug abuse and gambling. The decision was announced through a press release from the ministry today.

This move comes in response to the concerning rise in teenage gang activities and increased involvement of minors in drug-related offenses. The government aims to create a secure and healthy learning environment and protect students from activities related to drugs and gambling.

The Ministry stated that this decision is part of a broader government initiative to safeguard students. Further details regarding the committees' specific functions and operations are yet to be announced.

headline_marked: 624 [[detained in simultaneous Comilla police raids]] against teen gangs
headline: 624 detained in simultaneous Comilla police raids against teen gangs
summary: Police launched massive drives across the district to curb juvenile crime, following the killing of a 13-year-old boy.
details: A total of 624 suspected members of juvenile gangs were detained in separate drives across Cumilla yesterday, police said.
The operations were conducted by 18 police stations and various other units to prevent youths from becoming involved in crime and maintain law and order.
Most of the detainees were later handed over to their guardians after police obtained written undertakings that they would not engage in criminal activities in the future.
Police are currently scrutinising whether some of the detained youths were involved in drug-related offences and other crimes.
Detentions were high in several areas, including Kotwali Model (75), Daudkandi (59), Burichang (50), and Manoharganj (41).
In Daudkandi, 17 of the detained youths allegedly vandalised the police station, damaging tables, chairs, and a door, while chanting slogans against police.
Police officials stated that they are keeping the activities of juvenile gang members under close watch and such drives will continue to ensure public safety.
The crackdown has stepped up following the killing of Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, the 13-year-old son of a Comilla University teacher.
